titleTransition.method: In-process CGWindowList poll at 20ms (docs/verification/probes/window-title/, titlepoll), started before run_app and compared against the wall clock immediately after run_app returned.
titleTransition.conclusion: The title becomes non-idle DURING run_app and well before it returns — by 5.79s and 10.70s in two samples. The transition is not instantaneous with launch, so a readback taken at an arbitrary instant is not self-evidently safe; but at run_app's return the title is reliably settled.
titleTransition.limitation: The run_app return timestamps are UPPER bounds: they were taken by the controlling agent on the turn after the tool returned, so they include agent round-trip latency. More importantly, this method cannot observe the boundary that actually matters — whether the flip precedes the server's internal post-connection-proof readback point, which is inside the call and invisible from outside. The bounded poll in the design is therefore retained as the safe construction, not discarded on the strength of these margins.

deviceSwitchDefect.note: Gate 8.1 reproduced the A1 defect it exists to detect, live, against the installed v0.5.0 server.
sequence: run_app(device: fenix6xpro) -> ok, sessionId 1; window title = fēnix 6X Pro
run_app(device: fenix7s)    -> ok, sessionId 2, device 'fenix7s'; window title STILL fēnix 6X Pro
sim_status                  -> currentDevice 'fenix7s' while the window showed fēnix 6X Pro
sim_stop + sim_start + run_app(device: fenix7s) -> window title = fēnix® 7S
deviceSwitchDefect.conclusion: Both symptoms in the consumer report are confirmed on this machine: the launch is reported successful for a device the simulator never loaded, and sim_status echoes the requested device as though it were observed. The window title detects it; nothing else in the current tool surface does.
